name: Vibepollo
description: A fork-of-a-fork: Vibepollo builds on Apollo (itself a Sunshine fork), adding AI-assisted development, automatic virtual-display management, Windows Graphics Capture in Service Mode, and deep Playnite game-library integration. Windows-first in practice, even though the underlying Sunshine codebase is cross-platform.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: The project's own enhancements (virtual display, WGC service mode) are Windows-only; Linux/Wayland behavior isn't clearly documented

Tailscale Support.comment: No native integration; works over any reachable network

Open Source.comment: Fully open source on GitHub, in the same license lineage as Sunshine/Apollo

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: A dropdown lets you pick which display to stream; the virtual display auto-matches the client, but it's one display per session

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Inherited from the underlying Sunshine/Moonlight streaming protocol

H.265 Codec.comment: Includes fixes for false/incorrect HEVC support detection on headless setups

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Streams a single display/session, not isolated multi-user terminal sessions

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: Depends on host GPU encoder; the virtual display auto-matches the client's own refresh rate

Pre-Login Access.comment: Requires an active logged-in Windows session to capture from, like the Sunshine base it's built on

No Account Required.comment: Self-hosted with one-time PIN-based client pairing, no cloud account of any kind

Shared Clipboard.comment: Explicitly listed as a core feature (inherited from Apollo)

Windows: Host.comment: The primary, most developed platform — virtual display and WGC service mode are Windows-only features

macOS: Host.comment: Inherited from the base Sunshine codebase, but Vibepollo's own enhancements don't target macOS

macOS: Client.comment: Via Artemis (a companion Moonlight fork) or standard Moonlight clients

Linux X11: Host.comment: Inherited from Sunshine; Vibepollo's headless-specific fixes are documented with Windows in mind

Web Browser: Client.comment: The web UI is for configuration and client pairing, not for viewing the actual video stream in-browser

NVIDIA RTX 4090.comment: No official published benchmark table; performance follows the host GPU's encoder tier (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel)

Intel iGPU (QuickSync).comment: Intel hardware encoding is explicitly supported

Free Tier.comment: Completely free and open source, no paid tiers at all
